intro: The most common reason people in Crofton call out a plumber for leak detection isn't a burst pipe or a visible flood — it's a water bill that's crept up without explanation, or the faint sound of running water when everything's switched off. Hidden leaks are remarkably common here, particularly in the older housing stock that makes up much of the town. Whether it's a slow drip behind a kitchen unit, a weeping joint beneath a concrete floor, or a corroded pipe hidden within a stone wall, the damage tends to build quietly over months before homeowners notice. Getting a leak found and fixed promptly is one of the most cost-effective things you can do for your home.
localContext: Crofton has a real mix of property ages and construction styles, and each type brings its own leak-related challenges. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that are common across the town often have original or partially original pipework — lead, iron, or early copper runs that have seen decades of use and are starting to show their age. Joints that were sealed with outdated materials, pipes running through thick stone walls, and awkward layouts that were never designed with easy access in mind all make leak tracing more involved in these homes. On the newer modern estates in and around Crofton, the issues tend to be different — plastic push-fit joints that haven't been seated correctly, or underfloor pipe runs where a small fault can saturate a large area before anyone notices. Crofton also sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale gradually builds up inside pipes and around fittings over time. This narrows the internal bore, raises pressure, and puts additional stress on older joints — accelerating the kind of slow leaks that are easy to miss until the damage is done.
serviceDetail: A professional leak detection job in Crofton typically follows a clear process, starting with a conversation about what you've noticed — unusual damp patches, higher water usage, discolouration on walls or ceilings, or just a vague suspicion something isn't right. The plumber will then carry out a basic pressure test on your pipework to confirm whether a leak is present and get a sense of its severity. From there, the approach depends on the property. In older stone-built homes, acoustic listening equipment is often used to pinpoint the precise location of a leak within a wall or floor without unnecessary damage. Thermal imaging cameras can also be used to detect temperature differences that indicate where water is escaping. Once the leak is located, the plumber will talk you through the repair options before any work begins. For straightforward accessible leaks — a faulty joint, a corroded section of copper pipe, a failing compression fitting — the fix is usually completed in the same visit. More complex repairs in period cottages with concealed runs, or instances where flooring or wall sections need to be opened up, may require a follow-up appointment. After the repair, a re-test confirms the leak has been fully resolved, and any access points are made good where possible.
pricing: In Crofton, most straightforward leak detection and repair jobs come in between £100 and £350. A call-out with a basic pressure test and a simple accessible repair — replacing a joint or section of exposed pipe — typically sits at the lower end of that range. Where specialist equipment like acoustic detectors or thermal cameras is needed, or where the leak is hidden within a wall or under a floor, costs move towards £250–£500, reflecting the additional time and equipment involved. The age and construction of your property makes a genuine difference to price: tracing a leak through the thick stone walls of a period cottage in Crofton takes considerably longer than the same job in a modern new-build. Emergency call-outs outside normal hours will carry a premium on top of the standard rate.
whyLocal: Choosing a plumber who knows Crofton well is genuinely worth it for this type of work. Someone familiar with the town's older stone-built properties understands the quirks of thick-wall construction and the kind of pipework layouts common in period homes. They'll also know the typical pressure and water quality characteristics of the local supply, which matters when diagnosing whether limescale or pressure issues are contributing to the problem. A local tradesperson is also more likely to be available quickly — which counts for a lot when a leak is actively causing damage — and they'll have a reputation in the area worth protecting.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have a hidden leak in my Crofton home?
faqs.a: The most common signs are an unexplained rise in your water bill, the sound of running water when everything is off, damp patches on walls or ceilings, or soft spots in flooring. In older Crofton properties with stone walls, you might also notice efflorescence — white salt deposits — appearing on internal walls, which often indicates long-term moisture movement through the masonry.

faqs.q: Can leaks be detected without digging up my floors or opening walls?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Modern acoustic leak detection and thermal imaging equipment allows plumbers to pinpoint leaks with a high degree of accuracy before any physical investigation begins. This is particularly useful in Crofton's older stone-built homes and period cottages where opening walls unnecessarily could cause significant disruption and damage to original finishes.

faqs.q: Does hard water in Crofton make leaks more likely?
faqs.a: It can contribute to them over time. Crofton's moderately hard water gradually deposits limescale inside pipes and around fittings, which increases internal pressure and puts stress on older joints. It also accelerates corrosion in some types of pipework. Regular servicing and keeping an eye on water pressure can help catch problems before they develop into full leaks.

faqs.q: What happens if the leak is under a solid concrete floor?
faqs.a: Your plumber will use specialist detection equipment to locate the leak as precisely as possible before any work starts, minimising the area that needs to be opened up. Once the repair is completed, the concrete and any floor coverings are reinstated. In Crofton's modern estate homes with underfloor pipe runs, this is a fairly common scenario and experienced local plumbers handle it routinely.
